statement: The Virginia Consumer Data Protection Act applies to persons that conduct business in the Commonwealth or produce products or services that are targeted to residents of the Commonwealth and that (i) during a calendar year, control or process personal data of at least 100,000 consumers or (ii) control or process personal data of at least 25,000 consumers and derive over 50 percent of gross revenue from the sale of personal data (Va. Code § 59.1-576(A)).
caveat: § 59.1-576(B) exempts Commonwealth bodies, GLBA financial institutions and data, HIPAA covered entities and business associates, nonprofits, and institutions of higher education, and § 59.1-576(C) exempts listed data classes (health records, FCRA, DPPA, FERPA, employment-context data, and others). Both thresholds are narrowed by the § 59.1-575 definitions: a 'consumer' is a Virginia resident acting in an individual or household context (commercial and employment contexts are excluded) and 'sale of personal data' means an exchange for monetary consideration, with five listed exclusions. This repo does not determine whether the Act applies to a given business.
